standard.title: Exponent Laws
standard.description: establish and apply the exponent laws with positive integer exponents and the zero-exponent, using exponent notation with numbers
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can write numbers using exponent notation and connect powers of 10 to place value (from AC9M7N02, AC9M7N03). Students understand prime factorisation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students establish and apply the product, quotient, and power-of-a-power rules, and the zero exponent, using numerical examples and exponent notation.

nodes.label: Establishing the exponent laws from expanded form
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students derive the product of powers, quotient of powers, and power of a power rules from expanded form, and state each rule.
nodes.minimum_width: Derive and state the product rule (aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ) using at least two numerical examples.
nodes.typical_width: Derive all three laws from expanded form; state each rule; verify using digital tools; establish that a⁰ = 1 for any non-zero base.
wider: Investigate why a⁰ = 1 using the quotient rule: aⁿ/aⁿ = a⁰ = 1 — connect to the pattern of decreasing exponents.
Explore the pattern extending to negative exponents: what would a⁻¹ mean, following the sequence pattern?

response_modes.reason: Deriving the laws from expanded form requires an explicit step-by-step process. Students who jump to applying rules without derivation have fragile understanding and apply laws incorrectly to different bases.

success_criteria: Derives at least one exponent law from expanded form.
States all three laws and the zero exponent correctly.

nodes.label: Applying exponent laws in combination
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students apply the exponent laws individually and in combination to simplify numerical expressions, checking that bases are the same before applying.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply the product and quotient rules to simplify expressions with the same base.
nodes.typical_width: Apply all three laws in combination to simplify multi-step numerical expressions; identify when the zero exponent arises naturally; use digital tools to verify.
wider: Investigate expressions where multiple laws apply in sequence — develop a systematic order of operations for exponent simplification.
Explore how exponent laws apply in scientific notation contexts: multiply and divide numbers in scientific notation using the product and quotient rules.

response_modes.reason: Applying the laws in combination requires procedural fluency with each law before they can be chained. Errors typically arise from applying laws across different bases or confusing additive and multiplicative rules.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Scientific notation contexts offer advancing students rich application of the exponent laws — multiplying and dividing very large or very small numbers in science connects the abstract rules to meaningful computation.
success_criteria: Correctly applies each exponent law individually.
Applies laws in combination without confusing different-base expressions.
Does not apply exponent laws when bases differ.
